messages.subject: tilde problem and other problem
parts:
Hi all.

I have got a problem when there are tildes at axis in my ggplot2
scripts. R says that there is a multi-byte character in it. Curiously
it does not happen with all scripts, only with those created in
Windows. When I am in Linux, I have to copy and paste them in another
file in order to get them working. I have checked if there is any mark
in files (I use 'vi') created in Windows and they are completely
clean. Any idea?

Here is a reproducible example:

library(ggplot2)

p <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt, mpg,colour=factor(cyl)))+
geom_hline(yintercept=c(median(mtcars$mpg)),colour = "grey")+
geom_vline(xintercept=c(median(mtcars$wt)),colour = "grey")+
opts(legend.position='none', panel.background=theme_blank(),
axis.title.y = theme_text(size = 8, colour = 'grey40', angle = 90),
axis.text.y = theme_text(size = 8, colour = 'grey40',hjust=0.6),
axis.title.x = theme_text(size = 8, colour = 'grey40'),
axis.text.x = theme_text(size = 8, colour = 'grey40'),
axis.ticks = theme_blank())+
stat_smooth(method=lm, se=FALSE, colour="grey80")

comma2 <- function(x, ...) {
format(x, decimal.mark = ",", trim = TRUE, scientific = FALSE, ...)
}

q<-p + geom_point()+
labs(x = 'Taxa de Aprovação', y = 'Grau de Eficiência')+
scale_y_continuous(formatter="comma2")+
scale_x_continuous(formatter="comma2")

require("lattice")

pdfit <- function(f, ...) {
trellis.device(dev=pdf, theme="col.whitebg", ...);
print(f);
dev.off()
}

pdfit(q, file="aproveff3.pdf",width=6.2,height=3.831891223733)


When I try to run it, R shows the following message:

Error in source("aproveff3.R") :
invalid multibyte character in parser at line 19


BTW, I have another problem that is not related with ggplot2 or R but
maybe someone can help. The file created from that script I transform
to a .png file using the following command line:

gs -dSAFTER -dBATCH -dNOPAUSE -sDEVICE=png16m -dGraphicsAlphaBits=4 -
dTextAlphaBits=4 -r1200 -dBackgroundColor='16#ffffff' -
sOutputFile=aproveff3.png aproveff3.pdf

The graphic is perfect except the line generated by
"stat_smooth(method=lm, se=FALSE, colour="grey80")" that has some
"chops" in it (I don't know how to post an image to the group). I have
to say that the .pdf one is totally perfect. Any help on that too?

Thanx.

messages.author: 66a7bbbceef834e9
messages.subject: Re: tilde problem and other problem
parts:
Hi Arko, it sounds like a codification issue reading files from windows in linux. Linux uses utf-8 while windows uses ISO 8859. Maybe you are reading it with the wrong character set.


HTH
Luciano
